newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION - Wallaby coach Smith likened to Mains.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Wallaby coach Smith likened to Mains.

text.p: SYDNEY, July 16 - Wallaby coach Greg Smith is Australian rugby's version of former All Black coach Laurie Mains, according to noted commentator Spiros Zavos.
Zavos, in his regular Sydney Morning Herald newspaper column, said Smith was every bit like Mains, who guided the All Blacks for four years, culminating with the World Cup final loss in 1995.
"Smith's manner, that mixture of informed and somewhat testy comment, and the beleaguered air, reminded me of someone else," Zavos wrote.
"Then it came to me: Greg Smith is Australia's equivalent of Laurie Mains."

Smith, increasingly under fire for lacklustre performances by the Wallabies even when they win, is a noted fan of Mains, who also endured harsh criticism and poor results as he built a team for the 1995 World Cup.

When he came to the Wallabies' helm at the start of 1996, Smith told NZPA that Mains was the coach he most admired, primarily for his ability to struggle through adversity and produce one of the best rugby teams the world had seen.

Zavos believes Smith has modelled his performance on Mains, saying Smith faced the same task as Mains did on coming to power -- rebuilding a team who had won the World Cup (New Zealand in 1987 and Australia in 1991) but then disintegrated over the following four years.
"Both coaches began the renewal process by naming their best forward as captain," he said referring to Sean Fitzpatrick and John Eales.
"Both coaches identified first five-eighth as their critical problem."
Mains tried a number of candidates -- Walter Little, Grant Fox, Simon Mannix, Marc Ellis and Stephen Bachop before settling on Andrew Mehrtens after Fox retired.
Smith, without the retired Michael Lynagh, has used Scott Bowen, Pat Howard and David Knox before settling on Tim Horan for the time being.
"Like Smith, Mains was determined to have a tough pack. He clung to Richard Loe as a front rower even when Loe's foul play disgusted the world of rugby," Zavos went on.

"Last week, Smith was calling for the Wallabies to 'start an all-in brawl to get their message across'. And he is hinting at bringing back Michael Brial to ensure the Wallabies get their 'retaliation' in first."
Using large number of players was a criticism that had been levelled at both coaches.
"After three years of clinging to his job, Mains presented a team that should have -- but did not -- win the World Cup tournament.
"To his credit he left his successor John Hart with a better team than he inherited.

"Smith's record is, so far, better than that of Mains. A loss to the Springboks and three to the All Blacks on one side of the ledger are balanced by wins over England, Ireland, Wales, Scotland, France and South Africa.
"But will the 1999 Wallabies be a team to match the 1995 All Blacks, who became (under the gifted coaching of Hart) the Incomparables of 1996?"
